narration.full_text: Namaste students! In this section, we'll dive into the fascinating world of control and coordination in living organisms. We'll explore how different activities are regulated and integrated, ensuring survival and proper responses to the environment. Control and coordination is the process by which various activities of an organism are regulated and integrated. This allows the organism to respond appropriately to both internal and external stimuli. Think about it: living organisms are constantly performing multiple activities simultaneously. These activities must be carefully controlled and coordinated to maintain balance and ensure their survival in a dynamic environment. All living organisms continuously respond and react to changes happening around them in their environment. These changes that trigger a response or reaction from an organism are called stimuli. Common examples of stimuli include light, heat, cold, smell, and touch. Both plants and animals exhibit responses to these stimuli, though the manner in which they react can be quite different. In animals, control and coordination are primarily achieved through the collaboration of two major systems: the nervous system and the endocrine system. These two systems work together to ensure that all bodily functions are regulated and integrated effectively.
